en: Mayon Volcano in Albay is famous for its perfectly symmetrical cone shape, which you can clearly see from Legazpi City.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making its lower half subject to ocean tides.
Lake Taal in Batangas contains Volcano Island, which itself holds a smaller crater lake called Main Crater Lake.
The Rafflesia, found in the rainforests of Mindanao, produces the largest individual flower in the world, growing up to one meter wide.
Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea features massive coral atolls that rise directly from deep ocean waters.
Mount Pulag in Benguet features a mossy forest ecosystem where trees are constantly covered in thick, wet moss due to high cloud cover.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 cone-shaped limestone hills that turn brown during the dry season.
The Candaba Swamp in Pampanga acts as a natural flood basin that absorbs excess water from the Pampanga River during the rainy season.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, has enormous eyes that are actually larger than its brain to help it see at night.
The amihan wind brings cool, dry air from the northeast to the Philippines between November and February.
The Tiwi geothermal field in Albay naturally releases steam from the ground because magma heats underground water reservoirs.
Mangrove forests in the Philippines have specialized above-ground roots called pneumatophores that allow the plants to breathe in muddy, oxygen-poor soil.
